name: Myles Lozano
headline: Aerospace Engineering | Mechanical Engineering | Embedded Systems
shortBio: Dual-degree Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering student at Oklahoma State University building at the intersection of mechanical design, embedded systems, product development, and early-stage technology, with hands-on experience supporting military engine hardware and developing field-ready systems.
longBio:
I am a dual-major engineering student at Oklahoma State University studying Aerospace Engineering and Mechanical Engineering, with a minor in Electrical Engineering.

My experience spans product development, engineering design, prototyping, and early-stage system development. In Summer 2026 I was a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at GE Aerospace - Strother, where I created 18+ VGT inspection tooling concepts and led a Stage 1 nozzle flow investigation for military and commercial propulsion hardware, earning a GE Aerospace Impact Award. I have also worked on engine remanufacturing at Springfield Remanufacturing Corp., and I currently develop client hardware at the OSU New Product Development Laboratory.

At TriPoint Innovations, LLC, which I cofounded, I lead product design of Hunter Radar, guiding early-stage hardware from initial idea through prototyping and refinement, backed by a $75,000 USDA grant. I also lead engineering for OSU CEAT's 1st-place automated Homecoming display. I bring a strong work ethic, a rapid learning mindset, and eagerness to take on challenging technical problems.
